newsitem.title: USA: Puerto Rico tax break changes may hit MIA carriers.
newsitem.headline: Puerto Rico tax break changes may hit MIA carriers.

text.p: The phasing-out of some tax incentives for investment in Puerto Rico could drive business from the island and hurt the air cargo carriers that serve those businesses, experts said.
"Air cargo airlines as well as agents and shippers will be facing lowered expectation for growth," said Rich Cashman, head of Marketechs, an air cargo consultant.

The tax incentives, referred to as 936 for their U.S Internal Revenue Service code section, will be phased-out over the next 10 years and experts warn that the pharmaceutical, clothing, high technology and other companies manufacturing there may shift their production out of Puerto Rico.
The two South Florida airlines that stand to be hit the hardest are Arrow Air Inc., Miami and Amerijet International Inc., Fort Lauderdale, said Cashman.
"We are watching this closely," said Arrow spokesman Mike Clark, but "it is far too early to predict what might happen."

"I just don't think it will have much impact," said Pam Rollins, vice president Amerijet. "The companies have well- established businesses. Will they really move for the tax benefits? I don't visualize this having much impact at all."
The companies affected are looking at ways to reinstitute some of the tax breaks.

The manufacturers "with operations in Puerto Rico are exploring other alternatives, but it is too early to say what they might do," said Peter Holmes, head of the Puerto Rico USA Foundation, a trade group for companies with operations on the island.
Said Cashman: "air cargo traffic will be dampened as the gloomier climate for investment and expansion in the region settles in."
